abstract: We study primitive finite-order Hecke characters of $\mathbb Q(i)$ whose orders divide four, ordered by the norm of their conductor and including all dyadic local characters. For conductor at most $Q$, we prove a fourth central moment bound $Q^{13/9+\epsilon}$ at bounded height and an explicit low-height zero-density estimate. The density exponent is $3/5$ at $\sigma=5/6$, with a positive height power chosen after the requested loss. The density comparison adds information below Liu’s stated zero-free boundary $0.874886647\ldots$; benchmarks above it only compare methods. The arithmetic starting point is an ordinary common-coefficient polynomial mean $Q+Q^{2/3}L$, obtained by combining an existing inverse-pair estimate with the quadratic large sieve. We retain every local conductor component and every zero at a canceled prime when taking character ratios. Primitive Poisson summation then gives a Gram row-square bound $QZ+Q^{8/3}$. Hilbert duality and a finite restricted-row iteration convert this estimate into large-value bounds; a buffered scalar zero detector supplies an actual common-coefficient witness for the density application. The fourth-moment exponent improves the direct-square baseline $5/3$ for the identical conductor family. At $\sigma=5/6$, the corresponding second-moment detector gives density exponent $7/8$. We credit the earlier cubic conductor method and recompute its quartic input. Self-contained CPU controls verify finite local identities and exact rational exponent inequalities. These are family estimates, with no new individual zero-free half-plane or resolution of the Riemann hypothesis.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Clarify the density comparison against Liu’s prior finite-order zero-free half-plane, mark that region in Figure 1, and define the normalized inverse and full detector polynomials explicitly. Theorems and exponent formulas are unchanged.
title: Fourth moments and zero density for quartic Hecke characters ordered by conductor
